name: Steam Boiler
description: Industrial fire-tube boiler — monitor feed water flow, steam pressure, and stack temperature for tube rupture and over-pressure conditions

fault_explanations.pump_failure: Feed water pump failure — water supply to the boiler has stopped. Steam pressure is dropping as the drum level falls. If not corrected immediately the tubes will overheat and risk a tube rupture. The low-water cutoff should activate automatically.
fault_explanations.blockage: Steam line blockage — downstream restriction is causing pressure to build in the boiler drum while steam output flow drops. Pressure relief valves are approaching setpoint. Check the main steam valve, steam trap, or downstream process equipment for obstructions.
fault_explanations.cavitation: Cavitation at the feed water pump — suction pressure has dropped below the water's vapour pressure at the operating temperature. Vapour pockets form at the impeller eye and collapse violently, causing pressure oscillation. Check the deaerator level and suction strainer.
fault_explanations.fouling: Tube scale fouling — mineral deposits (primarily CaCO₃ and MgSiO₃) are building up on the water-side of boiler tubes. The insulating scale layer raises tube metal temperature while restricting water flow. Stack temperature is climbing as heat transfer efficiency drops. This accelerates tube creep and corrosion.
fault_explanations.thermal_runaway: Overheating — stack temperature has exceeded the critical limit. The burner may be over-firing or the tubes are scaling so severely that heat cannot transfer to the water. Tube metal temperature is approaching the creep range — risk of tube rupture. Reduce firing rate immediately.
fault_explanations.cooling_failure: Heat transfer failure — stack temperature is rising despite adequate feed water flow. The boiler tubes are not absorbing heat effectively, likely due to soot buildup on the fire side or severe scale on the water side. Combustion gases are bypassing the heat exchange surface.
